report:
### Executive Summary
Whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy shows promise as a supportive intervention, but direct evidence confirming that it prevents bone fractures specifically in osteoporosis sufferers remains inconclusive.

### Key Findings
* **Bone Mineral Density (BMD):** Vibration therapy provides mechanical stress that regulates bone metabolism, helping preserve or increase BMD in postmenopausal women as a safe supplementary treatment (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/endocrinology/articles/10.3389/fendo.2025.1611677/full; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139).
* **Fall and Fracture Risk Reduction:** WBV improves postural balance, motor capacity, and muscle strength. By preventing falls, WBV indirectly reduces fracture risk, particularly for individuals unable to perform vigorous exercise (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11914-015-0294-8).
* **Direct Clinical Evidence:** Robust trials demonstrating a direct reduction in fracture incidence among osteoporosis patients are lacking. Most current research evaluates healthy individuals or relies on surrogate markers like BMD and balance rather than verified fracture prevention (https://theros.org.uk/information-and-support/treatments-and-medicines/complementary-therapies-for-bone-health/vibration-therapy/).

### Conclusion
WBV therapy is a valuable complementary tool for improving balance and supporting bone density, but it is not yet proven to directly prevent fractures as a standalone osteoporosis treatment.
